references.text: The first time overseers (נֹגְשִׂים) are mentioned in connection with the Israelites' slavery in Egypt, where they were placed over the people to afflict them with forced labor.
God sees the Israelites' suffering under the overseers (נֹגְשִׂים) and hears their cry because of the slave drivers.
The continuation of this account where the overseers and foremen carry out Pharaoh's command and punish the Israelite labor leaders.
Moses' instruction to appoint judges and officers (שֹׁטְרִים) in Israel, using the same Hebrew word as for the Israelite overseers under Pharaoh.
A prophetic contrast where God promises that oppression will be replaced with peace, and overseers (נֹגְשִׂים) will be replaced with justice.
The use of נֹגְשִׂים (overseers/oppressors) as a description of those who rule over the people in a harsh manner.
A clear narrative and theological contrast: Joshua uses supervisors to lead God's people to freedom, directly opposite to Pharaoh, who used them for oppression.

Theological contrast: Pharaoh uses a command to destroy the people (Ex 5:6), while God uses a command to sanctify them (Ex 19:10); this highlights the difference between human oppression and divine salvation.
